title: Jaguars 53-man roster projection as training camp approaches
description: How will the Jaguars' 53-man roster shake out? We take a look ahead of the start of training camp.
fullText:
Training camp is around the corner.

The Jacksonville Jaguars will soon be embarking on the month long journey to prepare themselves for the regular season and beyond.

Ahead of the start of training camp and the preseason, here's a look at the potential 53-man roster based on what we've seen from the offseason.

Rank Em!: 5 most important Jacksonville Jaguars for 2026 include the big names

While Travis Hunter will be listed twice on this roster, he is counted only once (cornerbacks).

Projected on roster: Trevor Lawrence, Nick Mullens

Cuts: Carter Bradley, Joey Aguilar (R)

Observations: Lawrence's job is safe and it'll take a lot for Bradley or Aguilar to usurp Mullens as the backup. However, the battle for third string QB could heat up throughout training camp. Bradley is the incumbent but the Jaguars promote competition at all levels. It'll be something to watch, especially during joint practices and preseason games.

Projected on roster: Chris Rodriguez Jr., Bhayshul Tuten, LeQuint Allen, DeeJay Dallas

Cuts: Ameer Abdullah, J'Mari Taylor (R)

Observations: We have yet to see Rodriguez on the field after his injury sidelined him during offseason workouts. The thought is that the Jaguars will use a by committee approach to their running game. Tuten and Allen are expected to step into larger roles in their second season with the team. An underrated battle might be between Dallas and Abdullah as the team's kick returner. Whoever wins that battle will secure their spot on the roster.

Projected on roster: Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr., Parker Washington, Travis Hunter, Josh Cameron (R), CJ Williams (R)

Cuts: Brady Boyd (R), Chandler Brayboy, Tim Jones, Ben Patterson, Trebor Pena (R), Austin Trammell, Michael Wortham (R)

Observations: What a crowded room. Meyers, Thomas and Washington are surefire starters. Hunter's defensive usage might bring his offensive snaps down some, opening the door for someone to get some extra reps. Williams had an impressive offseason and will likely carve out a role with the team. Cameron has special teams value as a returner, likely cementing his spot.

Projected on roster: Brenton Strange, Nate Boerkircher (R), Quintin Morris, Tanner Koziol (R)

Cuts: Patrick Herbert, Hunter Long, Ethan Conner (R)

Observations: Are philosophical changes coming for Coen's offense? That's a joke, but I am curious if we'll see a set with all four of these players on the field at the same time. This position is pretty straightforward with both rookie tight ends making the team in addition to the two guys who received contract extensions from the team this offseason.

Projected on roster: Cole Van Lanen, Ezra Cleveland, Robert Hainsey, Patrick Mekari, Anton Harrison, Walker Little, Emmanuel Pregnon (R), Jonah Monheim, Wyatt Milum, Chuma Edoga

Cuts: Jerome Carvin, Trystan Colon, Ricky Lee, Jimto Obidegwu, Garrett DiGiorgio (R)

Observations: I think the team will opt to keep 10 offensive linemen. As they try to solidify the five best starters, they'll need several players who can play multiple positions in reserve spots. As Van Lanen returns from his injury, we'll likely see different combinations across the line throughout camp.

Projected on roster: Josh Hines-Allen, DaVon Hamilton, Arik Armstead, Travon Walker, Ruke Orhorhoro, Albert Regis (R), BJ Green II, Danny Striggow, Wesley Williams (R)

Cuts: Keivie Rose, Matt Dickerson, Zach Durfee (R), T.J. Bollers (R), Quinton Bohanna, Jalen Hunt (R), Quindarius Dunnigan, Bryan Thomas Jr. (R)

Observations: This group has heavy expectations placed on their shoulders. With a healthy Travon Walker back in the ranks, position flexibility is key here as well. Several of the players here can play inside or out, giving the team the bodies needed should injuries arise.

Projected on roster: Foye Oluokun, Ventrell Miller, Dennis Gardeck, Branson Combs, Jack Kiser, Jalen McLeod

Cuts: Yasir Abdullah, Parker Hughes (R)

Observations: Another position group that's pretty straightforward. With McLeod back in the mix Abdullah is on the outside looking in. Hughes is the last man in, so he's first man out. He'll be a practice squad candidate though.

Projected on roster: Travis Hunter, Montaric Brown, Jourdan Lewis, Jarrian Jones, Jabbar Muhammad

Cuts: Keni-H Lovely, Christian Braswell, Preston Hodge (R), Devon Marshall (R), Dane Jackson

Observations: Muhammad had as good of a camp as any player on the roster. It's with that logic that the 2025 UDFA makes the team. Lewis and Hunter missed the entire on-field portion of offseason workouts, but they're projected starters. Brown was brought back to be a starter and Jones could find himself amongst the starters depending on how Lewis' recovery goes. Braswell would likely need to have a better camp than Muhammad to make the roster. Lovely and Hodge are longshots who could find themselves in a competition if the team keeps an extra corner.

Projected on roster: Eric Murray, Antonio Johnson, Caleb Ransaw, Rayuan Lane III, Jalen Huskey (R)

Cuts: Devin Neal Jr. (R), Cam'Ron Silmon-Craig, Trevian Thomas

Observations: Murray and Johnson are the likely starters here with Ransaw potentially pushing his way into a starting role. Lane is a special teams ace and Huskey is a Day 2 pick from this year's draft. It'd take a something terrible for him to be cut from the roster. Neal, Thomas and Silmon-Craig are likely battling for a practice squad spot after roster cuts are made.

Projected on roster: Logan Cooke, Cam Little, Ross Matiscik

Observations: The kicker who has the two longest field goals in league history is safe. The highest-paid long snapper in league history is safe. The player with the highest net punting average in league history is safe. This is the most clear cut position grouping.

title: Marquis Clark talking trash to get playing time with Tennessee basketball
description: Tennessee basketball freshman guard Marquis Clark knows playing time may be hard to come by this season. He's developed a plan to get on the floor.
fullText:
Tennessee basketball freshman Marquis Clark wants to be annoying.

It's nothing personal. But as Clark sits behind a roster full of guards and ball-handling wings, he's trying to find ways to get on the court.

His solution? Talking trash. It's an old trick he and fellow Chicago native Dai Dai Ames have relied on during the Vols' summer practices.

"I'd say Dai Dai," Clark said on July 23 about who else talks the most trash. "We're from Chicago, so we like to talk stuff and get in people's head. That's what gets us going. Yesterday, Dai Dai was going at Miles (Rubin), talking smack to him. That's what we do."

Clark is a smaller, 6-foot-1 guard with a penchant for scoring. At Whitney M. Young High School, he broke the all-time scoring record with 1,983 career points, surpassing the previous record set by NBA first-round draft pick Quentin Richardson.

Scoring alone, though, won't get Clark on the floor on a Rick Barnes roster.

"Defense for sure," he said about where his game has developed most. "Being a pest, that's how I'm going to get on the court, so I've got to keep that up. I feel like that's been the best thing I've picked up."

Clark isn't the only player that has had to work on his defense. Barnes has had to teach his schemes to an almost entirely new group, a group that was specifically recruited for its scoring prowess.

"I think that guys have started to understand more and more what we're looking for, and way more defensively than anything," Barnes said. "What made it so difficult is that we had so many new guys. The only really active player from last year was DeWayne (Brown II), with Troy (Henderson) being out. In the past, our older players helped us with that guys came in. Every player we've recruited to come in here has had to come in and learn to do what we want to do."

Adjusting to Barnes, and college basketball, hasn't been easy for Clark. In one previous practice, he was punished to the Versaclimber, an intense cardio machine, between "six or seven" times, he recalled.

Clark has leaned on Brown and Henderson as the two returners from last season who also dealt with Barnes as freshmen.

"I've learned a lot," he said. "When I came in, I didn't really know what to expect. They were the first two guys I went to since they were here last year. I've definitely learned a lot, and I keep asking questions."

Clark is jostling with the other freshmen to be this season's Brown. Barnes said he thought about redshirting Brown last fall before the forward became the "biggest surprise" on the roster and quickly carved out a spot in the rotation.

Clark may be slotted behind other experienced guards like Ames, but he wouldn't have it any other way.

"We signed up to play against the best of the best," Clark said about the freshman class. "For all of us, we came in with the mindset that we want to get on the court, so we're going to compete against whoever."

title: USA250: The 10 greatest Nevada college athletes ranked
description: Nevada and UNLV are the two prominent colleges in the state and they lead our list of 10 best college athletes from the Silver State.
fullText:
In choosing the 10 greatest collegiate athletes to play in the state of Nevada, we’re pretty much limited to two schools - the University of Nevada and the University of Nevada-Las Vegas.

That isn’t to say there aren’t plenty of worthy candidates from those institutions, but the biggest names who played their home games in the Silver State did so for the most part in the traditional revenue sports, and wound up either heading south to Las Vegas or north to Reno.

With apologies to Wolf Pack fans, this list is going to favor the Rebels bit thanks to its hoops pedigree. But we think we’ve chosen the top candidates from both locales.

The brightest of the stars from UNLV’s glory days was enshrined in the National Collegiate Basketball Hall of Fame in 2019. Over his two seasons with the Runnin’ Rebels that included the 1990 NCAA championship and a Naismith Player of the Year honor a season later, he averaged 21.6 points and 11.2 rebounds before embarking on his NBA career.

While football often took a back seat to basketball at UNLV, Cunningham nevertheless left his mark in college before his lengthy NFL tenure. He threw for 8,020 yards and 59 touchdowns while also doubling as the punter from 1982-84. In his senior season, Cunningham threw for 24 scores as the Rebels set a school record with 11 wins.

Nevada’s innovative pistol offense needed the right man at the controls, and Kaepernick did it better than anyone. From 2007-10 he amassed 14,200 yards of total offense and surpassed 2,000 yards passing and 1,000 rushing for three consecutive seasons with the Wolf Pack.

The power forward known as "The Hammer" was a first-team All-American during the 1986-87 season while leading the Rebels to the Final Four. He set a single-season scoring record with 903 points that year and led the school to 93-11 record in his three seasons with three NCAA Tournament appearances before being selected No. 2 in the NBA draft.

Inducted into the Nevada hall of fame in 2025, Snyder led the Wolf Pack to the Western Athletic Conference regular season and tournament titles and the school's first Sweet 15 appearance as a senior in 2004. He was named WAC player of the year that season and scored 1,404 career points during his Reno days before being selected in the first round of the NBA draft.

The floor general for those UNLV Final Four squads also has a place in the school’s hall of fame. He handed out 838 assists and snared 275 steals over his four seasons with the Rebels. Anthony was a three-time, all-Big West selection and a third-team All-American in his senior season.

A standout infielder with the Rebels, Williams compiled 58 home runs and 217 RBI during his three seasons at the school. His best campaign was his final year when he hit 25 long balls and drove in 89 runs while being a first-team All-American selection. Williams was the No. 3 overall pick in the 1986 MLB draft and would go on to a 17-year career with 378 home runs.

Moore had one of the great seasons in men's collegiate golf in 2004 as he won the NCAA individual championship in addition to taking the U.S. Amateur title and victories in the the U.S. Amateur Public Links and the Western Amateur. The following year as a senior, Moore won the Haskins and Nicklaus Award with a scoring average of 69.29, the second-lowest in NCAA history.

UNLV’s all-time scoring leader in women’s basketball, Frohlich averaged 21.2 points and 10.1 rebounds with the Rebels from 1998-2002. She was a three-time Western Athletic Conference player of the year and third-team All-American as a senior. Frohlich competed for her native Germany on the national team and now operates a sports academy in California.

Kaepernick’s running mate in the Wolf Pack backfield was arguably just as instrumental to the team’s success during its epic 13-1 season in 2010. A third-team All-American as a senior, e recorded 5,159 yards from scrimmage, 4,588 of those rushing, and scored 53 total touchdowns for his Nevada career.

title: How Louisiana football won over local commit 2027 DE Ansinneo Charles
description: LRCA football's star defensive edge Ansinneo Charles is staying home committing to UL football. Here's why.
fullText:
Lafayette Renaissance Charter Academy football’s Ansinneo “AJ” Charles knew when he stepped foot on the University of Louisiaiana-Lafayette’s campus, that he was home.

The three-star senior defensive edge was one of Acadiana’s top defensive prospects from the Class of 2027 and had his pick of the litter with double-digit Division I offers. In the end, Charles decided to stay close to home, committing to the Ragin’ Cajuns on July 17.

“When I went for my official visit, my mom loved it, I loved it and they treated everybody like family,” Charles said. “It was nice and the coaches, they really played a big part in my decision, the way they talked about me and the way they want to implement me.”

Listed at 6-foot-5 and 220 pounds, Charles is one of seven commits hailing from the boot and one of two from the 337 area. He chose Louisiana over offers from Mississippi State, Syracuse, Louisiana Tech and Texas State, among others. According to Charles, the personal relationships built with UL football coaching staff would be the difference maker. The Cajuns had their sights set on him from the start of their recruitment of the Class of 2027.

“Before they were offering the 2027 class, I talked to Coach Des [Michael Desormeaux] and they were like ‘You’re going to be one of the first ones we offer’ and eventually they offered me,” Charles said. “From there, I would say it was the communication and that bond that I shared with UL over schools like Mississippi State.

Mississippi State is a hell of a school, good team, good conference, good everything but like I said, it was the bond and stuff that won me over at UL.”

Along with the strong connection Charles built with the Cajuns coaching staff, he also feels like he’ll be a great addition to their defense come fall 2027.

“The position they said I would be it’s most likely going to be rushing off the edge majority of the time, but then I also can cover like what I’m doing now,” Charles said. “ They compared me to a few guys that came through the program and all the things like that and they said I would probably get to be a true freshman.”

Having the possible opportunity to see the field as a freshman is a huge draw for players like Charles within Group of 5 programs like UL, where youth shines through compared to Power 4 programs. Before he’ll be working for his shot to make an immediate impact on the fied for the Cajuns, Charles will look to lead LRCA to a deep postseason run in the upcoming 2026 season.

“Oh, we got a lot cooking,” Charles said of the Tigers during the offseason. “We playing against some tough competition, but we’ve been working all summer since January. So everything we’re about to get it what we deserve.”

title: USA250: The 10 greatest college athletes from Nebraska
description: As part of USA TODAY Sports' USA 250 initiative, here's a look at the top 10 greatest college athletes to ever play in the state of Nebraska:
fullText:
Nebraska is a fascinating state to delve into in regard to college sports history, as it has a burgeoning sports scene without the imposing influence of professional sports.

The University of Nebraska's Memorial Stadium has sold out since the 1960s. The College World Series takes place in Omaha. Nebraska women's volleyball holds the world record for attendance at a women's sporting event.

And it isn't just a matter of circumstance. The programs built the loyalty. The Tom Osborne Nebraska-Oklahoma-Barry Switzer football rivalry is the stuff of legend, the 1990s Cornhuskers are still spoken of in reverential tones. Creighton basketball went from Missouri Valley powerhouse to Big East staple. And Nebraska women's volleyball has one of the most passionate followings among college sports as a whole.

From all of that loyalty is borne legendary figures. Across the state and across sports, Nebraska has the athletes to run with nearly any state in the country. Paring that list down to 10 proved to be an extremely difficult task. But here are the 10 Nebraska college athletes who managed to set themselves apart.

Nebraska of the 1990s was dominant. And Tommie Frazier was one of the team's great players in the decade. After he got his feet wet as a freshman, Frazier came into his own as a sophomore. Though he rarely threw the ball in Tom Osborne's ruthless triple option offense, but he passed for 3,521 yards in his career and added 1,955 yards and 36 touchdowns on the ground. But Frazier's legacy defies stats: Nebraska won 36 of 37 games in his final three seasons. The lone loss came to Florida State at the end of the 1993 season in the Orange Bowl that was a matchup of two unbeatens. Frazier would then lead the Cornhuskers to back-to-back titles the next two season and finish runner-up to Eddie George in the voting for the 1995 Heisman Trophy.

USA 250 LISTS: Alaska | Alabama | Arizona | Arkansas | California | Colorado | Connecticut | Delaware | Florida | Georgia | Hawaii | Idaho | Illinois | Indiana | Iowa | Kansas | Kentucky | Louisiana | Maine | Maryland | Massachusetts | Michigan | Minnesota | Mississippi | Missouri | Montana | Nebraska | Nevada | New Hampshire | New Jersey

Born in Omaha in 1935, Bob Gibson is one of the most dynamic pitchers in baseball history. His stuff is the stuff of legends, and he got his start with the Creighton Bluejays. A two-sport athlete, Gibson played baseball and basketball for his hometown university. He finished his career on the hardwood as the school's third-leading scorer at the time with 1,272 points. Unfortunately, his baseball stats are lost in the annals of history, it's known he was an outfielder and a pitcher for Creighton. Gibson had a legendary pitching career with the St. Louis Cardinals, and was named to Creighton's Hall of Fame in 1968.

When you think about hard-nosed Huskers, you think about Mike Rozier. After setting the single-season school record with 1,689 rushing yards as a junior in 1982, he shattered his own mark the following season as part of one of the greatest offenses in college history. Rozier put up an absurd 2,148 yards and an NCAA-record 29 touchdowns on the ground on his way to winning the 1983 Heisman Trophy. That Nebraska offense averaged over 50 points per game with Rozier serving as the focal point, and though it came up short of a national title with an Orange Bowl loss to Miami, it's remembered as one of the great seasons in Nebraska football.

PROGRAM RANKINGS: Top 25 | Big Ten | SEC | ACC | Big 12

Ask someone born in the '90s the most dominant defensive player they watched in college growing up, and dollars to donuts Ndamukong Suh's name is going to come up. One of the most overpowering linemen in history, Suh turned otherwise-stalwart offensive linemen into sleds. Suh's 2009 season is the stuff of college football legend: He finished fourth in Heisman Trophy voting, the best at the time for a solely defensive player since Steve Emtman in 1991 after logging 85 tackles with 20½ tackles for a loss and 12 sacks. Suh missing out on the Heisman was widely regarded as a death knell for the hopes of a solely defensive player winning the trophy, and he remains a Nebraska legend to this day.

Johnny Rodgers isn't just etched into the fabric of Nebraska. He's woven into the tapestry of college football. A receiver, running back, and return specialist, record after record fell before Rodgers' speed. A Walter Camp Player of the Year and Heisman Trophy winner in 1971, Rodgers finished his career with the two highest all-purpose yards seasons in Nebraska history, along with the record for most career all-purpose yards. He still holds the record for career receiving touchdowns and ended his time on the gridiron with the most points accounted for in Nebraska history. Often considered among the best return men in college football history, Rodgers was precursor for the athlete position in college sports.

Eric Crouch evokes one of the last gasps of an era of greatness for Nebraska football. Crouch led the Big 12 in rushing touchdowns in each of his final three seasons and posted a 35-7 record as a starter. He had a dominant senior campaign in 2001 to win the Heisman Trophy, edging out Florida quarterback Rex Grossman. For the season, Crouch rushed for 1,115 yards and 18 touchdowns and threw for 1,510 yards, while leading the Cornhuskers to the Bowl Championship Series title game in the Rose Bowl. Though Nebraska would lose to Miami (Fla.) in his final game, Crouch's legacy has endured as one of the most dynamic athletes in Cornhusker football history.

While Nebraska football is a dynasty, Nebraska volleyball is an institution all of its own. The Cornhuskers are five-time national champions and have four championships since the turn of the century. Pavan is one of the most decorated volleyball players in Nebraska history. She was a four-time first-team All-American and set multiple records with the Cornhuskers while making Lincoln a destination for volleyball. Pavan helped Nebraska to a national championship in 2006 and four consecutive Big 12 titles. She is quintessentially Nebraska volleyball, and volleyball is quintessentially Nebraska.

Why wouldn't Nebraska get two volleyball players on this list? Joining Pavan is Jordan Larson, who was also part of the 2006 championship team. Larson was a three-time All-American and had over 1,000 kills and digs in her Nebraska career. Her best season was in 2008, when she earned multiple accolades before becoming an Olympic star as well, culminating in a gold medal win in Tokyo in the 2020 Summer Games.

Fresh off her college career when she was a four-time first-team All-American, Frahm is already a Nebraska softball legend. Born in Papillion, Frahm started her career at Oklahoma, winning two national championships with a 44-2 record as the star pitcher for Sooners. Frahm transferred to Nebraska after her sophomore season, but was injured in her first game in 2024. She returned the following year to help Nebraska to the super regionals for the first time since 2014. Frahm was national player of the year as a senior, leading the Cornhuskers to their first Women's College World Series appearance since 2013,. A true two-way superstar, she posted a 47-14 record pitching over two seasons at Nebraska with an ERA of 1.44. She slugged 1.418 as a Cornhusker with 43 home runs.

title: 'Not your job': Usman Tariq's bold message to opponents over questions being raised on controversial bowling action
description: Pakistan spinner Usman Tariq has hit back at opponents questioning his bowling action, insisting that only umpires and officials have the authority to judge its legality.
fullText:
'Not your job': Usman Tariq's bold message to opponents over questions being raised on controversial bowling action originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Pakistan spinner Usman Tariq hit back at players questioning his bowling action, saying such concerns should be left to umpires.

Tariq revealed Tom Banton’s gesture during a match prompted his response, urging players to show professionalism.

The mystery spinner has faced scrutiny over his unique action, with opponents questioning its legality.

MORE:Gambhir under scanner as Laxman-Iyer deliver Zimbabwe whitewash

Pakistan’s mystery spinner Usman Tariq has firmly retaliated against the criticism surrounding his unique bowling action, stating that the players of the opposing team need to focus on their games and not get into his business regarding his bowling action.

Tariq, known for his unusual stop-and-pitch delivery method, has become a topic of discussion after players have expressed their doubts about whether his bowling method is within the laws of cricket.

Speaking on Beard Before Wicket, Tariq alleged that Tom Banton made some gesture towards him in the middle of the game, which he considered to be crossing the line.

In the ILT20 2026 Qualifier 1 match in Abu Dhabi, playing in as a late replacement player for Lockie Ferguson for Desert Vipers, MI Emirates batter Tom Banton appeared to accuse Tariq of "throwing" after being dismissed by the Pakistan spinner.

"I think one day, Tom Banton made that gesture to my face. I felt like, 'This is not your job. You are not the one who will pinpoint these things'," Tariq commented on that.

"The umpires are already there and they are the ones who are going to question me. So being a professional player, I think we should be way more mature and intelligent to have the knowledge of the rules of this game."

Interestingly, the comments were aired just a day before Tariq endured a difficult outing in The Hundred, where he went wicketless and was smashed for back-to-back sixes by Tom Moores during Birmingham Phoenix's defeat to Southern Brave.

MORE:Tom Moores smashes Usman Tariq for back-to-back sixes

Talking about gestures and issues related to bowling actions, the Pakistani spinner concluded that cricket players should be more professional.

"It's better to give a message to the board that we are professionals and we do not have that character to do such kind of negative stuff," Tariq added.

"I felt at that time, when you are doing those types of things (gestures), it shows what character you have."

The bowler further said that although he usually does not like to get into any on-field confrontations, he could not help retaliating against the England batter.

"Whenever these happen, honestly, I don't respond. But when Tom Banton did that to my face, I also responded to him with some good words."

MORE:Hardik Pandya trade: MI want CSK duo as part of swap deal

Tariq's bowling action has proved to be one of the major talking points about the player, especially due to the unique bowling action that he possesses. He has received queries regarding his bowling action in the past, and there have been instances where players like Tim David have raised eyebrows about his bowling action while facing him.

However, Tariq maintains that his bowling action has already been cleared and according to him, anything regarding the matter of the legality of the bowling action should be done by the umpire instead of other players.

Queries on bowling actions in cricket are not new, and it is completely acceptable for players to bring their queries to the notice of authorities. However, the matter of whether the bowling action is legal lies in the hands of the umpire and match officials, not in the gestures of players in the middle of a game.

title: Why do minor leaguers keep chasing the MLB? Ask Smokies infielder Ed Howard
description: Former Cubs first-round pick Ed Howard's career hasn't unfolded the way he wishes it did. Why Howard continues to chase his MLB dream against the odds
fullText:
Ed Howard knows what people see when they look at his career: a hometown kid from the South Side of Chicago, selected 16th overall by the Cubs, and once destined for an infield spot at Wrigley Field.

They also see the injuries that followed.

What many don't see is why the Knoxville Smokies infielder keeps playing the sport he dedicated his life to at 5 years old, even as the odds grew longer.

"I probably could have walked away from the game, and nobody probably would have got mad at me," Howard told Knox News. "But that never occurred. I never even thought of that because I wanted to reach my dream."

Somewhere along the way − in a career defined by surgeries, setbacks and nearly four years of rebuilding − Howard stopped worrying about whether baseball had treated him fairly and instead focused on where it could still take him.

Acceptance is something he never expected to learn. And after a two-month stint in a hospital bed, he came to understand a lesson many athletes learn much earlier: Talent alone is not enough to shield a career from adversity.

"I just always wanted to write my own story," he said. "I don't want the injury to define it."

The South Bend Cubs had erased a five-run deficit against the Fort Wayne TinCaps on May 10, 2022, when Howard hit a grounder to shortstop. With one out in the ninth inning, he collided with the first baseman, fell to the ground and tried to stand back up. He couldn't move.

Trainers helped him to the clubhouse, where his mother and grandmother found him distraught in a ripped jersey.

"I was just angry, upset," Howard said. "Who was I upset at? I was just upset at the world. I didn't know."

Howard tore the labrum in his left hip, dislocated the joint and fractured the posterior wall in his pelvis. Eight days later, a titanium plate was inserted with screws.

He spent two months glued to a hospital bed, receiving blood-thinner injections in his stomach and watching his left leg shrink from not being used. He had to re-learn how to walk.

The physical recovery was measurable. The mental recovery was not.

Howard spent the first 18 years of his life believing hard work could solve almost anything. Baseball wasn't part of his family, but he was always taught that "if you really want something, just put in the work."

That's what carried him through the 2014 Little League World Series and later helped him become one of the top prep players in the 2020 MLB Draft as a shortstop from Mount Carmel High School in Chicago.

But the injury wasn't something Howard could overcome with effort. When you're out of action as a baseball player, he said, that's "all that's running through your mind."

His mind was ready to rehab and never talk about the injury again. But recovery doesn't follow a definite timeline.

"I wanted to come out like a rocket and just be the same 18-year-old kid that I was," Howard said. "But it doesn't work like that."

When he returned ahead of schedule roughly 10 months later, he collected two doubles as part of a three-hit night. Though it seemed like Howard had returned from the outside, the underlying challenges persisted.

"I'm limping," he said. "I'm struggling in my apartment. I got to get up and use the restroom in the middle of the night and I can't get there."

Patience was the biggest lesson Howard took away from his injury. Prior to getting hurt, everything with baseball was always moving forward.

"At 18," Howard said, "you want everything when you want it."

Rather than dwelling on why the injury happened, Howard began asking what could still become of it. He hit his first home run at Covenant Health Park in Knoxville on July 9, proving to himself that he could still play the game at a high level.

Faith deepened during the years away from the field, Howard said, and his family became the foundation. The internal belief never left.

"Nobody knows you more than you know yourself," he said.

Howard stopped worrying about outside opinions. He believes in who he was. The work ethic, mindset and drive remained consistent, he said: "I'm still the same guy."

As the hometown kid with all the potential, the 24-year-old smiles when asked about pressure. He welcomes the feeling.

"Pressure is a privilege," Howard said.

Once a high-profile shortstop, Howard hopes to play in games where expectations are high again. Expectations mean people still believe in him.

"I pray that one day there are more pressure moments in my career," he said.

Howard still believes he can make it to Wrigley Field. Though injuries changed his body and altered his timeline, his performance is meant to satisfy an audience of one.

"At the end of the day," he said, "I'm really doing this to prove it to myself."

His present-day self looks back at the young Howard − angry at the world in the Four Winds Field locker room in South Bend, Indiana. On the winding road back from his 2022 injury, he has discovered everything happens when it's supposed to happen. He just had to accept it first.

"I just want to keep going," he said, "until I can look up and almost smile and laugh at him."

title: USA250: The 10 greatest New Jersey college athletes ranked
description: Princeton and Rutgers are the two biggest university represented on our list of the 10 greatest college athletes from the state of New Jersey.
fullText:
From Ellis Island to the Jersey Shore to Asbury Park and the Stone Pony, the very town where Bruce Springsteen first lit up the stage, New Jersey is home to many things.

It’s also home to a deep roster of NCAA programs, including eight Division I universities, an Ivy League lacrosse powerhouse in Princeton and the "Birthplace of College Football" at Rutgers in New Brunswick. Two of its mid‑majors, St. Peter’s and Fairleigh Dickinson, have etched their names into March lore as unforgettable tournament Cinderellas.

And that’s only the surface of the state’s athletic legacy. Some of the nation’s top professional stars first built their careers at colleges across The Garden State.

So, here is the 100%, completely definitive (and surely unanimous) top 10 athletes to compete in college sports in New Jersey:

Bradley is considered one of the greatest athletes in Princeton athletics history and one of the most prolific men's basketball players of his time. A three-time All-American, Bradley is the program’s all-time points leader with 2,503 career points scored, a record he set without making a single 3-point shot and in just three years with freshmen ineligible to play. He’d also captain the United States Olympic men’s basketball team at the 1964 Tokyo Summer Olympics, where they won gold, while still in college. Highlights of his career include leading Princeton to its only Final Four in 1965 when he scored 58 points against Wichita State in the third-place game, which remains the second-highest total in tournament history. After completing his player career, he was a Rhodes Scholar, member of two New York Knicks championship teams and a U.S. Senator for the state of New Jersey.

Lloyd wasted no time becoming one of the best collegiate women’s soccer players in the country during her time at Rutgers, a path that led her to becoming one of the most decorated United States women's national team players.  The New Jersey product led the Scarlet Knights to the Sweet 16 as a freshman in what was the program's second-ever tournament bid. while setting program's single-season points record as a freshman at 37, with 15 goals and seven assists leading the way. A two-time All-American and the 2004 Big East midfielder of the year, Lloyd finished her career as the program’s all-time points (117) and goals scored (50) leader. Both records remain today. She is also tied for third with 15 game-winning goals scored.

USA 250 LISTS: Alaska | Alabama | Arizona | Arkansas | California | Colorado | Connecticut | Delaware | Florida | Georgia | Hawaii | Idaho | Illinois | Indiana | Iowa | Kansas | Kentucky | Louisiana | Maine | Maryland | Massachusetts | Michigan | Minnesota | Mississippi | Missouri | Montana | Nebraska | Nevada | New Hampshire | New Jersey

Dick Kazmaier is not Princeton’s only Heisman Trophy winner but is the last player from the Ivy League to receive college football's highest individual honor. Known to be a weapon in the Tigers’ single-wing offense, Kazmaier, who played halfback, kicker and quarterback, finished his career as Princeton’s all-time rushing leader (1,950 yards) and ranked second in passing (2,404 yards). In his Heisman Trophy season in 1951, Kazmaier led the Tigers to a perfect 9-0 season and No. 6 national ranking while rushing for 861 yards and nine touchdowns and throwing for 966 yards and 13 touchdowns.

Rice is not only one of Rutgers' greatest running backs, but one of the top players the program has ever produced. Coming off a standout freshman season with just over 1,110 rushing yards, Rice exploded for 1,754 yards and 20 touchdowns on 335 carries the next season. That’d earn him a seventh-place finish in the Heisman Trophy race. He led the nation the following season with 2,012 rushing yards and 25 touchdowns, earning first-team All-America honors and being selected as a Doak Walker Award finalist. He finished his Rutgers career with three consecutive 1,000‑yard seasons — a first in program history — and totaled 4,926 rushing yards and 50 touchdowns (49 rushing).

If Bradley was the greatest to step on the court for Princeton, then Sellers certainly was that for Rutgers. While Dick Vitale was an assistant and head coach at the school, he averaged 21.0 points and 9.8 rebounds in four seasons with the Scarlet Knights. He led Rutgers to its first ever NCAA Tournament and Final Four appearance his junior and senior seasons, respectively. Sellers averaged 19.2 points and 10.2 rebounds per game and was a second-team All-American in his senior season in 1976, the same year the Scarlet Knights finished with a 31-2 record after winning their first 31 games. Sellers would complete his career as Rutgers' all-time scoring and rebounding leader with 2,399 points and 1,115 rebounds. He was also a third-team All-American in 1975.

PROGRAM RANKINGS: Top 25 | Big Ten | SEC | ACC | Big 12

One of the more recognizable United States men’s national team players from the 1990s, Lalas serves the same recognition amongst former Rutgers athletes. A third-team All-American as a sophomore and junior, he won the Hermann Award — soccer’s version of the Heisman Trophy — during his senior season as he helped Rutgers to a 15-match unbeaten streak and the program's first No. 1 ranking. He led Rutgers to a combined record of 71-15-8 in his four seasons "On The Banks." He also led the program to three NCAA tournaments, which included appearances in the national semifinal in 1989 and the national championship game in 1990.

Known primarily as a second baseman in his Hall-of-Fame Major League career, Biggio spent three seasons as Seton Hall’s catcher and helped the program to a 121-55 overall record and a Big East title in 1987. A two‑time All-Big East first‑team selection and All‑American as a senior, Biggio hit .342 for his career and still holds the program record for triples (18). He also ranks second in runs scored (194) and is tied for fifth in home runs (27).

Hubbard is one of the greatest to ever put on the Princeton lacrosse jersey and one of the best goal scorers in college lacrosse history. A three‑time All‑American, Hubbard delivered one of the program’s defining moments in its rise to a national powerhouse with his overtime game‑winner in the 1996 NCAA title against Virginia, giving Princeton its first national title. He’d then help lead the Tigers to the next two Ivy League and national championships, strengthening their rise and dominance in the sport under Bill Tierney. Hubbard finished his career as Princeton’s all-time leading goals scorer with 163 goals and is now second all‑time in career goals and sixth in points (211).

Todd Frazier was a productive bat for the Scarlet Knights from the moment he arrived on campus, Frazier drove in 36 runs and hit nine home runs as a freshman. His best season came as a junior in 2007 when he blasted a program single-season record 22 home runs, drove in 65 runs, while leading Rutgers to a Big East tournament title and an NCAA berth. He went 13-for-25 at the plate with 12 runs scored, five walks and three home runs in six games at the Big East tournament that season. Just the third Rutgers player taken in the first round of the MLB draft, he ranks second in career home runs (42) and first in runs scored (210).

A multi-sport athlete, Pearce, who later changed her surname to Rampone, showcased her versatility at Monmouth, where she played soccer, basketball and lacrosse. It was on the soccer pitch where she quickly became her signature. Pearce dominated the Northeast Conference, a four-year career with the Hawks that helped her eventually make the U.S. women’s national team and, ultimately, win four Olympic medals. A two‑time Northeast Conference player of the year winner, she still owns the school career records for goals (79), assists (54), and points (212).

title: Wakefield hooker Smoothy to join Perth
description: Wakefield Trinity boss Daryl Powell said the club would like to keep Smoothy but he's been released on compassionate grounds.
fullText:
Wakefield Trinity have confirmed hooker Tyson Smoothy will join new NRL side Perth Bears at the end of the season after being released from his contract on compassionate grounds.

The 27-year-old Australian joined Trin on a three-year deal for this campaign but head coach Daryl Powell said earlier this month that he would be leaving at the end of 2026.

Smoothy has scored four tries in 21 appearances in all competitions to help Wakefield to second in Super League.

"Tyson has made a fantastic contribution to the squad this season and while we would love to keep him, we are conscious of family circumstances and his desire to return home," director of rugby Ste Mills told the club website.

"Tyson's attitude and performance have been first class all year and the club is supportive of his decision".

Smoothy will join the newly formed Bears for their inaugural season alongside Leeds Rhinos trio James McDonnell, Harry Nerwman and Mikolaj Oledzki.

title: PGA Tour FedEx Cup points leaders mostly unchanged after 3M Open
description: The PGA Tour's FedEx Cup points leaders were virtually unchanged after the 3M Open and Scottie Scheffler is still in command.
fullText:
Jackson Koivun did a bit more than win his first PGA Tour title on July 26 at the 3M Open, in his third professional start.

His 500 FedEx Cup points for winning put Koivun right on the FedEx Cuo playoff bubble.

Koivun is 70th on the points list with 525.2. That's the final spot that will qualify for the FedEx Cup Playoffs in two weeks after the final two regular-season events, the Rocket Classic in Detroit (July 30-Aug. 2) and the Wyndham Championship in Greensboro, N.C. (Aug. 6-9).

The top 70 will advance to the first of three playoff events, Aug. 13-16 at the FedEx St. Jude Classic at TPC Southwind in Memphis.

Koivun's lead isn't much. He's 2.695 points ahead of No. 71 Andrew Putnam, 20.08 points clear of No. 72 Mac Meissner and 36.669 points ahead of No. 73 Johnny Keefer.

If Koivun misses the cut this week at the Detroit Golf Club, players down to No. 111 Mark Hubbard could pass him with a top-10 finish or better.

Scottie Scheffler, who led the FedEx Cup points list through the end of the regular season three of the last four years (winning in 2024), posted his fifth runner-up finish and 11th top-10 at the 3M Open and remains comfortably ahead on the points list. Scheffler is up 794 points over Matt Fitzpatrick and 1,037 over Cameron Young.

The only movement among the points leaders was Gary Woodland going from 29th to 25th with a top-10 at the 3M Open, and Hideki Matsuyama going from 37th to 36th with tie for third.

Scheffler isn't scheduled to play again until the St. Jude Classic, and his closest pursuers are evidently conceding him another regular-season title. Fitzpatrick isn't entered this week and Young, who is playing the next two weeks, couldn't catch Scheffler if he won both to earn a maximum of 1,000 points.

There could be some jockeying behind Scheffler this week. The Rocket Classic has a decent field, drawing 22 of the top-50 on the points list, led by Young, No. 4 Wyndham Clark, No. 7 Si Woo Kim and No. 12 Akshay Bhati.

title: Nick Saban is a 'Mike Elko guy' and feels Texas A&M 'reloaded" in 2026
description: On the Pat McAfee Show, Nick Saban stated that Texas A&M has "reloaded" this offseason, and is on track to be a CFP contender in 2026.
fullText:
After making the College Football Playoff for the first time in program history, Texas A&M coach Mike Elko, entering his third season at the helm, saw a record 10 players selected in the 2026 NFL Draft and will return 65% of the 2025 roster, led by starting quarterback Marcel Reed, who threw for a career-high 3,169 yards, 25 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions.

On defense, losing unanimous All-American Edge Cashius Howell, who led the SEC with 11.5 sacks last season, stings, but was expected, and among A&M's 17 transfer portal additions this offseason, former Northwestern Edge Cashius Howell and several defensive line additions shore up the NFL departures, on paper, at least.

With Marcel Reed returning for his second full starting season, he'll be throwing to star junior receiver Mario Craver and Alabama transfer Isaiah Horton, who brings more size at 6'4", and should open up the middle of the field for Craver, Ashton Bethel-Roman, and Terry Bussey to thrive in short to intermediate throws.

This week, Mike Elko, alongside Marcel Reed, linebacker Daymion Sanford, and safety Marcus Ratcliffe, made the trip to Tampa (FL) for SEC Media Days to preview the 2026 season, and former Alabama coach Nick Saban, who has been a fan of Mike Elko since he was hired after the 2023 season, also attended the event as an analyst for ESPN/SEC Network, while making an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show, where he explained by he believes the Aggies have 'reloaded" to make another CFP run.

“Well, I’m a Mike Elko guy in terms of you know what he’s done at A&M,” Saban stated on The Pat McAfee Show. “They had 10 guys drafted. That’s more than they’ve ever had. They’ve got some of the highest rated recruiting classes, which they’ve never had in the past. Or when they did, they fell apart for whatever reasons, they’ve won more games. They play better defense. He’s one of the best defensive coaches in the country, scheme-wise, I think.

“And I think they’ve reloaded. I think they got some good players coming back. I think Marcel Reed is a really, really good quarterback who puts a lot of pressure on the defense. And I think they did a good job in a portal, and they did a good job of recruiting. I think they’re going to be one of the teams that people need to contend with in the SEC.”

Texas A&M's 2026 schedule is tough, facing road tests vs. LSU, Missouri, Alabama, South Carolina, and Oklahoma before hosting the Texas Longhorns at the end of the regular season, but given the defensive depth and Marcel Reed's experience under center, and after falling to Miami 10-3 in the first round of the CFP, Mike Elko bluntly stated “I show them our trophy case and it’s empty,” when asked about what keeps his team motivated heading into the new campaign.

title: Scottie Scheffler remains money in the bank on the PGA Tour earnings list

fullText:
Scottie Scheffler posted his fifth second-place finish on the PGA Tour on July 26 in the 3M Open. Rookie Jackson Koivun was rock-solid and didn't open the door for Scheffler by making mistakes down the stretch at the TPC Twin Cities, so Scheffler settled for another runner-up check ($959,000) while Koivun made $1,584,000 for his first PGA Tour title.

That gives Scheffler nearly $17 million in earnings this season and with all of his closest pursuers taking the week off, he increased his lead over No. 2 Cameron Young to nearly $3 million, and his margin over No. 3 Matt Fitzpatrick to more than $6 million.

Young is playing the next two weeks, in the Rocket Classic and the Wyndham Championship, where he is defending his title. He would have to win both tournaments (collecting $3,150,000 if he does) to pass Scheffler heading into the FedEx Cup Playoffs, where purses in the first two events, for official money (the FedEx St. Jude Classic and the BWM Championship), will be $20 million, with $3.6 million for the winners.

The PGA Tour money race will end after the first two playoff events. The Tour Championship, which pays the winner and the FedEx Cup champion $10 million, does not count for official earnings.

Scheffler is seeking his fifth consecutive PGA Tour money title, which would be a Tour record. He's currently tied with Tiger Woods (1999-2002) and Tom Watson (1977-1980) for the most consecutive years as the leading money winner.

title: Infantino tells Fifa critics to 'meditate, pray or watch football'
description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino tells critics to "meditate, pray or watch a football match" instead of "spreading hate and false rumours" about him and the World Cup.
fullText:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino has told critics to "meditate, pray or watch a football match" instead of "spreading hate and false rumours" about his leadership, the governing body and the World Cup.

In a 15-slide post on his personal Instagram account - reposted to Fifa's eight million followers - Infantino addressed "those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens" to affirm his belief that, while they were "busy planting seeds of hate", Fifa was delivering the "greatest event on earth".

He said the World Cup "celebrated humanity at its best", adding that the 2026 tournament had "100% safety and security, only joy and happiness".

Infantino downplayed several of the tournament's high-profile controversies and hailed the involvement of Iran, who featured at the World Cup despite their ongoing conflict with co-hosts the United States, as a success.

He said Fifa "worked tirelessly to unite two countries at war", with Iran entering the country "without incident or conflict".

His comments are in stark contradiction to those of Iran's head coach Amir Ghalenoei, who said his team were the "most oppressed" at the World Cup.

Infantino's 'time is up' with Fifa - La Liga boss

The country that doesn't play football... yet

Iran faced visa delays, "integral" members of their backroom staff were denied entry to the US and fans had their allocation of tickets revoked, while Iran also had to move their training base from Tucson, Arizona to Tijuana, Mexico following a multitude of logistical issues in the build up to the tournament.

They later also encountered restrictions on their movements as they travelled between their training base and group matches in Los Angeles and Seattle.

Such issues were not unique to Iran, with fans from Haiti, Senegal, and Ivory Coast impacted by travel bans imposed by the Trump administration, while Somali referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the US - despite holding a diplomatic passport and a single entry US visa - because of his "association with suspected members of terror organisations".

Infantino wrote: "You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world. Because football unites the world, and it was impressively demonstrated this summer."

Doubling down on the tournament's safety, Infantino said there were "zero incidents, zero violence, just joy, emotions, happiness, unity, and togetherness".

However, Fifa is investigating Argentina's actions after players and backroom staff were involved in altercations with Spain's players after losing the World Cup final. It is also investigating allegations of racist abuse towards American social media influencer IShowSpeed, while supporters were arrested at multiple matches - including following England's semi-final against Argentina in Atlanta.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials were also controversially present at World Cup stadiums.

Infantino also addressed criticism surrounding the standard of officiating at the tournament, in particular concerns about political interference after USA forward Folarin Balogun was made available for their last-16 tie when his one-match ban was suspended by Fifa - following the intervention of US President Donald Trump.

Of the 191 other red cards shown at a men's World Cup, only one other player has escaped a suspension.

Uefa said the decision had "crossed a red line", labelling it "unprecedented, incomprehensible, and unjustifiable", while the Norwegian Football Federation is considering filing a formal complaint to Fifa's ethics committee.

Infantino, however, argued that such decisions are not out of the ordinary, claiming similar rulings are "routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide".

He added: "It's curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising."

The International Olympic Committee has said it will not investigate Infantino for any possible breaches of political neutrality, stating the complaint levelled by human rights campaign group FairSquare falls outside the jurisdiction of its ethics commission.

Infantino's advice to his opponents was "to show some love" and "respect" to a tournament where "people came together as families, as fans, as one".

"To everyone who missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the celebrations, the laughter, the crying, the deception and the joy. To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents and parents come together for the beautiful game... sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all," Infantino wrote.

"While they celebrated, you were busy planting seeds of hate. Our world needs love, not hate; tolerance, not division; celebration, not mourning.

"To those spending their time and energy hating us, please take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray or watch a football match and truly observe the faces, the eyes, the emotions.

"Because only our beautiful game can deliver such an extraordinary show, a show where everyone becomes one and reconnects as humans.

"I am incredibly proud, as Fifa President, to have contributed, even a little, to this show. It's a great feeling."

title: Will Titans add any more players before training camp?
description: The Tennessee Titans could be looking to add more veteran talent to their roster before the 2026 season kicks off.
fullText:
It’s hard to believe that the Tennessee Titans will be on the field this week, and the 2026 season will finally be underway.

General manager Mike Borgonzi has done a masterful job at remaking the Titans roster over the offseason, and now new head coach Robert Saleh will have a chance to build them back into contenders. The big question is: Are they done adding competition to the roster?

A man named Cameron from Kentucky asked Jim Wyatt a solid question about possible additions in his weekly mailbag, and the answer was interesting.

Question: Hey Jim, do you think the Titans will add a veteran to the team heading to training camp?

Jim: Yes, at several positions along the way.

The Titans have already been active, adding defensive back Nazeeh Johnson and offensive tackle Zachary Thomas since rookies reported to the team facility on Thursday; moves that coincided with the team placing JC Latham and Amani Hooker on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. Taking Wyatt at his word, who else could be on the Titans' radar?

Looking at the players still available, two names come to mind: defensive backs Ifeatu Melifonwu and Kenny Moore. Tennessee has added some new faces to the secondary, but would definitely have room for some more competition and depth. While both of those players have different skill sets, they both have the ability to fill a role heading into the season.

title: 9️⃣ players to watch as the 2026 MLS Season returns
description: The 2026 World Cup is over, and we bring our attention back to Major League Soccer as we kick off the second half of the season. Here are some of the stars and breakout candidates who could shape the ...
fullText:
The 2026 World Cup is over, and we bring our attention back to Major League Soccer as we kick off the second half of the season.

Here are some of the stars and breakout candidates who could shape the second half of the season.

Inter Miami vs. Columbus on August 1 at 7:30pm ET. Watch live on Apple TV

New York Red Bull vs. Orlando City on August 1 at 7:30pm ET. Watch live on Apple TV

Chicago vs. Charlotte on August 1 at 8:30pm ET. Watch live on Apple TV

📸 Charlotte Wilson - 2026 Getty Images

One of the breakout stars in the West was tipped to perform highly at the World Cup, and with his former USMNT head coach-for-a-father watching, he did!

Midfielder Sebastian Berhalter impressed under Mauricio Pochettino, notably featuring in all five World Cup games and registering a goal plus an assist against Turkiye. That made him the first American in the modern era to record one goal and one assist in a World Cup match.

He already has 10 combined goals and assists in 14 MLS appearances this season, something he'll look to build on after gaining some confidence seeing his stock rise.

One of the biggest stories following the resumption of the MLS season is Inter Miami's signing of Casemiro. The five-time Champions League winner arrives in South Florida as another marquee addition to a star-studded squad, with hopes of helping Miami strengthen their push for MLS Cup.

The Brazilian could well make his debut this weekend after completing his move late last week, bringing a wealth of experience and winning mentality to Nu Stadium.

Casemiro made more than 120 appearances for Manchester United, winning the Carabao Cup and FA Cup during his time at Old Trafford. While his impact won't be measured in goals, his ability to control games, break up attacks and lead by example could prove just as valuable as Miami chase more silverware.

One of the biggest headlines as we return to the MLS season was Chicago's signing of Robert Lewandowski from Barcelona. The 37-year-old is the latest to come to America as a blockbuster transfer, hoping to help the Fire rise from third to first.

Lewandowski was denied a debut against Thomas Müller's Whitecaps due to smoky weather conditions, so it remains to be seen how he will kick off this new chapter.

He scored 14 goals from 31 appearances for the Blaugrana last season and walked away with a stunning record of 120 in 193. Though it's not really about how many he'll score for Chicago, rather, it's when. Everyone will be on high alert to watch his first hit the back of the net.

One of the youngsters who impressed in the first half of the season was Kevin Kelsy of the Portland Timbers. And he's already back up and running after the restart!

At just 21 years old, the Venezuelan centre-forward is impressing at the club, having scored 26% of their overall goals this season. He netted twice against Seattle Sounders, the first a looping header and the second a quick reaction to poke the ball home after crashing the box.

The brace sees him lead Portland's scoring charts this season, and after impressing against a rival, we're sure he will be flowing with confidence in the second half showing.

📸 Shaun Botterill - 2026 Getty Images

Naturally, how can we not mention Lionel Messi? The Argentina captain went all the way to the 2026 World Cup final while staying in contention for the Golden Boot. His ever-reliable presence for the national team is something we expect to continue for Inter Miami.

The Herons sit in second place in the Eastern Conference, largely thanks to Messi's brilliance. He already has 12 goals and seven assists after only 14 appearances this season.

That said, it will be interesting to see whether the 39-year-old experiences any fatigue as he re-enters the regular season. World Cup players are often given deserved breaks, and if Miami allows Messi to take a temporary vacation, who will step up in his absence? Without his impact, will the Herons struggle to fight for first?

A second headline signing heading into the back half of the season is Antoine Griezmann joining Orlando City. The Frenchman arrives in the United States after an impressive final season in Spain, where he registered 14 goals and eight assists across all competitions.

The Lions will look to the 35-year-old's storied experience to help lift them up from 13th in the table after just four wins so far. That poor form sees the club sit third last in the Eastern Conference.

That said, Griezmann has said he's prepared to be a leader for Orlando. "I want to win the championship, score goals, provide assists, encourage kids to play football and make them Orlando City fans," he said. "I came for all of this: I want to take Orlando City to the top of football in the United States."

📸 Dustin Satloff - 2026 Getty Images

Another youngster with his name in lights during the first half of the season was Julian Hall of the New York Red Bulls. And he's perhaps the most talked-about teenager currently in MLS.

The 18-year-old has a stunning 13 goal contributions (nine goals and four assists) from just 15 appearances. Add to that, there are also three other goals from two U.S Open Cup showings. Such numbers look like that of a veteran centre forward, rather than a high-school graduate.

After feeling refreshed from the break, it's time to see whether or not he will continue generating such hype.

After an early World Cup exit, Son Heung-min appears to be back and ready to put his best foot forward with LAFC.

The 34-year-old was a staple creative presence for the club prior to the international break, registering nine assists to help them sit third in West. That includes a statement showing against Orlando, where he produced five alone!

Now, however, Son appears hungry for goals. He scored his first of the season during the first game back against rivals LA Galaxy. Perhaps an early elimination from the World Cup and some rest was just what he needed?

📸 Alex Slitz - 2026 Getty Images

After an impressive run to the Round of 16 with Canada, defender Richie Laryea will be a player with the weight of BMO Field on his shoulders.

The veteran right-back demonstrated his veteran persona at the World Cup by playing a full 90 minutes in almost every one of Canada's games. A five-game starter, the earliest he was ever substituted off was the 78th minute.

TFC's injury issues before the break have left them struggling in 12th place in the East, but Laryea is the voice and presence at the back who can guide the team up the standings if and when he's at his best.

Looking at his stats, he has 15 goals and 26 assists in 155 appearances across all competitions for the club. He was also selected as an MLS All-Star. Will the hometown talent rise to the occasion in the second half of the season?

title: Diomande agrees Real Madrid terms as PSG step away
description: RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande agrees personal terms with Real Madrid after Paris St-Germain withdraw their interest.
fullText:
RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande has agreed personal terms with Real Madrid after Paris St-Germain withdrew their interest.

The 19-year-old Ivory Coast international was previously a target for Liverpool, who had an initial bid of £69m rejected in June, as well as PSG.

Liverpool then moved on to other targets, and PSG have now opted against entering a bidding war with Real.

PSG are said to have had a final £102.5m bid rejected for the teenager on Sunday.

Madrid have since agreed personal terms, said to be modelled on England midfielder Jude Bellingham's contract as they are incentivised on performances and effectively improve year-on-year.

Real will pay more than £100m for Diomande, who joined Leipzig from Spanish club Leganes last summer on a five-year deal.

'Everything I do is for you' - how tragedy is driving Diomande

Sources close to Real say key negotiators Jose Angel and Juni Calafat have been scouting Diomande for about five years, but were not reactive to Diomande's World Cup performances.

PSG had been frontrunners for the Ivorian until Real registered their interest, and they confirmed their withdrawal from the race on Sunday.

"The asking transfer fee and salary demands were completely disproportionate and distortive - and PSG will not break its principles of rational financial management and squad balance," the French club said.

"As a two-time consecutive Champions League winner and the most successful club in recent years, PSG will also not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents - and will instead calmly and confidently continue its transfer planning."

Leipzig have tried hard to keep the forward in Germany but regard the interest in Diomande as extraordinary, so have found it difficult to reject the interest - and potential record sale price - from Europe's elite clubs.

Diomande was the Bundesliga's young player of the season for 2025-26, having scored 12 goals and registered eight assists last term.

He moved from his native Ivory Coast to an academy in the United States in 2025 before joining Spanish side Leganes.

title: Who has the best college football stadium? Our top 25 rankings starts with LSU
description: Across the country, there are notable college football stadium that welcome fans on weekends in the fall. What are the best ones? Here's our list of 25:
fullText:
Few topics in college sports will divide respective fans than discussion the merits of their football stadiums. Saturdays in the fall are full of things that supporters hold dear. The traditions of game day, the pageantry and the success of their teams are something to be treasured by students and alums.

But we still accepted the challenge of trying to identify the 25 best stadiums with 10 staffers from USA TODAY Sports weighing in with their perspective using their own criteria. Some valued the visual element at top their list. Some considered the traditions or the difficulty of experience for opponents.

The final list includes locales from across the country in conferences big and small. The SEC dominates the representation with the Big Ten following behind in second. But there are plenty of are others included. Here’s the top 25 that is sure to inspire debate from readers:

A night game in Baton Rouge is an animal unlike any other. Bear Bryant described Tiger Stadium as “the worst place in the world for a visiting team.” LSU fans specialize in tailgating, full of culinary delights and plenty of imbibing. Then the game starts with the hostility on display that gives opposing players and fans something to forget. One thing to remember? The singalong for "Garth Brooks and "Callin' Baton Rouge."

The Horseshoe is one of the great venues in college football and one of the toughest places to win. The Buckeyes have lost just three games at home since 2016. Two of those losses have come in the rivalry against Michigan. Basically, any trip to Columbus with a crowd of more than 100,000 mostly against your team is as close to a guaranteed loss as you’ll find in the Power Four.

There are few better spectacles than Penn State's annual "White Out" games. It's especially intimidating in the evening when fans dress in white to provide visitors with an unsettling, eye-popping backdrop. Combined with the deafening roar provided by 100,000-plus fans, this makes Beaver Stadium one of the elite settings in the FBS.

Kyle Field supplies the SEC’s most singular experience. Yeah, there are some odd chants, routines and hand signs from the school's Aggie Yell Leaders. But the 12th Man is indefatigable, and the Aggies storming out of the tunnel to “POWER” before kickoff, while the stadium shakes, creates a scene suited for football heaven. A handful of SEC venues are tougher on road teams, but few stadiums are as memorable as this massive cathedral, especially when the fans sway in unison to the "Aggie War Hymn."

Size doesn't matter in the case of Autzen Stadium. While only boasting a capacity of 54,000, Oregon's home field is one of the classes of the Big Ten and toughest places to place. The Ducks have lost just twice at home since hiring Dan Lanning in 2022. This stretch rivals the most dominant run of play at home in program history, a 21-game winning streak under former Chip Kelly that ended with a loss to Southern California in 2011.

The environment "Between the Hedges" has made the Bulldogs nearly unbeatable at home under coach Kirby Smart. While the literally barking from Georgia fans doesn't always rattle your eardrums, Sanford Stadium can rumble when challenged. Georgia’s .918 home winning percentage during the Kirby Smart era is a credit to the program Smart built. It’s also a credit to Bulldogs fans.

STADIUM RANKINGS: Big Ten | SEC | ACC | Big 12

Simply put, Neyland Stadium is "a different type of loud," which is how former Oklahoma quarterback Baker Mayfield described playing there. And when the home team is thriving and “Rocky Top” plays on a loop, it’s pure psychological torture. Former Notre Dame quarterback Brady Quinn called it “the loudest place I ever played.” So loud, he said, the ball would tremble on the turf between plays.

There might be no other stadium that is a pictorial stand-in for college than the "The House that Rockne Built." Looming outside the stadium wall is the mural of "Touchdown Jesus" that overlooks the field. Lines and lines of some of the sport's most memorable coaches and players. National championships galore. While the vibe might be different than that seen at some of the larger SEC fields, no one can deny that Notre Dame Stadium occupies a special place in the sport's landscape.

You want history? How about the field where both Bear Bryant and Nick Saban walked the sideline while winning national championships by the bunches? It's also one of the toughest places to win. Alabama is 65-3 at Bryant-Denny the past 10 seasons. When 100,000 sets of crimson-and-white pompoms start shaking in the stands, you know: It’s over.

Florida fans singing Tom Petty's "I Won't Back Down" before the fourth quarter might be a new tradition. It's also peak college football. The Swamp can roar with the best of them, even if the Gators haven't matched their glory years in recent seasons. Consider last season: Florida went 4-2 at home, including an upset of Texas, and 0-6 away.

If you're looking for a stadium with a specific identity, Clemson Memorial Stadium has plenty to offer. There's one of the most raucous atmospheres in the ACC with more than 80,000 fans backing the home team. Between the Death Valley moniker, Howard's Rock, and the run down "The Hill," not to mention Clemson's historical success, it's hard to top the intimidation factor on college football Saturdays.

As great as the Big House is, size doesn't always matter the most. The largest venue in college sports is also the largest by seating capacity in the Western Hemisphere and the third largest in the world. At times, the Wolverines appreciated when the 100,000-plus crowd can influence the visitors, though bowl layout means the noise never quite seems to match the number of fans in the seats.

Nestled among the mountains in Provo, Utah, LaVell Edwards Stadium provides an intimidating presence for visiting teams with the crowd right on top of the field. There are not many panoramic views better in college football with one of the notable features being Y Mountain rising above the stands with a logo painted on its slopes that mirrors the one on BYU helmets. For those inclined to hike to the Y, you can do it with some effort. The path is short but very steep.

Husky Stadium might not register among college fans as one of the loudest stadiums in college football, however it absolutely stands with the elite when Washington is playing well. Fans watching on television can detect cameras shaking from the sound and raucous fans. But this ranking isn't just about sound. Husky Stadium also is one of the sport’s most beautiful backdrops and one of the coolest traditions: the “sailgating” boats checking out the action from Lake Washington.

Another place that has seen its home team have better days, Jordan-Hare still is regularly packed with Tigers fans who turn up the volume and influence the game. And how do you top a pregame ceremony with War Eagle flying around the stands? It's a truly unique environment, and nobody beats Auburn at swag surfing.

When talking about Lane Stadium, you begin with the start of the game. One of the great entrances in the sport takes place with Metallica's "Enter Sandman" blaring on the speakers and fans jumping up and down. The scenery surrounding Blacksburg provides spectacular fall colors that may not be appreciated on television. Should the Hokies return to the glory days of Frank Beamer, the fans will have played a significant part.

Not many places celebrate a touchdown better than Oklahoma with two Shetland ponies named Boomer and Sooner pulling a stagecoach across the field to celebrate. It's a portrait of Americana. The "Palace on the Prairie" lags a bit behind the stadiums with six-figure capacities, but it can still have its moments of urging on the home team to success and causing issues for the visitors.

Rice-Eccles Stadium is one of the few college football stadiums that have hosted an opening ceremony of the Olympics, but it mostly is one of the more difficult places for opponents to play. Helped by a student section dubbed the Mighty Utah Student Section, Utah boasts a 47-13 record at home since 2016, and the mark is more impressive at night with 29 wins in 35 games under the lights in the past 10 seasons.

The Badgers might have taken a step back in their success on the field, but the traditions at Camp Randall remain elite. None is more memorable than the “Jump Around” stampede at the end of the third quarter, which began in 1998 and was the soundtrack to the Badgers’ development into a powerhouse under former coach Barry Alvarez.

Occupying a picturesque location along the Hudson River, Michie Stadium sits in the middle of the United States Military Academy. There are not many better scenes in college football than the march-on with the Army cadets in formation prior to kickoff. You're experiencing patriotism and tradition rolled into one. The Black Knights might not be the best team on the field, but that's a bonus to an afternoon worth experiencing.

Sometimes it's something not part of the game that makes a stadium unique. One of the best scenes in college football comes at the end of the first quarter of Iowa home games. “The Hawkeye Wave” has players and fans turn to wave to the patients at Stead Family Children's Hospital overlooking the stadium. Kinnick is also a difficult place to play with the Hawkeyes compiling a 27-8 mark at home since 2021.

Admittedly, the Texas fans don't consistently produce a decibel level to match the capacity of more than 100,000. But for big games, the environment can be impressive. Texas is 13-1 at home since joining the SEC. As a certain Texas supporter who’s often found along the sideline would say: All right, all right, all right.

Let's be clear: The scene at the Rose Bowl is unlike any other when it hosts a game on New Year's Day. The scene for a Bruins home game lacks the same pageantry and tradition because the atmosphere is more muted with fewer fans in attendance and games not timed to have the sun set over the San Gabriel Mountains at the optimal time. But it's still worthy of inclusion for the shear history that drips from the time you make your way up to the stadium until you leave your seat at the end of the game.

Death. Taxes. A sellout for a Nebraska home game. Those are three things that have been certain since the start of the school's attendance streak in 1962. Despite the Cornhuskers being less significant on the field, this is one of the most iconic spots in college football. The fans provide one of the unique features of support when they release red and white balloons after the first Nebraska touchdown, though the tradition occurs less frequently.

Long one of college football’s most underrated venues, Williams-Brice is getting overdue respect the past few years. Never mind that South Carolina isn’t a blue blood or that they copied the hedges look of Georgia. When “Sandstorm” plays and those white towels wave, or when the crowd turns up the decibels on third down, you know you’re at a special place that packs a punch.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Who has the best college football stadium? Our top 25 rankings starts with LSU

title: Free cycling festival to celebrate Tour of Britain
description: Families will be able to take part in free cycling-themed activities in Hull and Blackpool.
fullText:
A free cycling festival will take place in Hull and Blackpool to celebrate the 2026 Tour of Britain men and women's races.

The women's race gets under way on 19 August, while the men's race starts on 2 September.

Families will be able to take part in cycling-themed activities in Blackpool on 20 August and Hull on 4 September from 11:00 until 14:00 BST on both days.

Jonathan Day, director of events at British Cycling Ventures, said last year's festival "brought the community together, creating a real showcase of what the joy of cycling can bring to people".

The women will race through Cockermouth, Clitheroe, Blackpool, Mold, Llandudno, Llanidloes and Hay-on-Wye, before finishing in Royal Leamington Spa on 23 August.

In Blackpool, the festival activities will open before the race finishes outside the Solaris Centre, on New South Promenade.

For the men's race, riders will travel through Lincolnshire, East Yorkshire and North Yorkshire, before finishing in Scotland on 6 September.

At Hull's East Park, those attending the festival can watch the race depart in the morning before enjoying activities, including cycling in the park.

Hull City Council said there would be a limited number of bikes for children and adults to hire, so participants have been encouraged to bring their own bikes.

There would also be adaptable bikes, suitable for riders of all abilities, the authority added.

Deputy council leader Jackie Dad said: "There will be an incredible buzz in East Park as we watch the professionals set off and then it is time for our own residents to take to the circuit.

"It's a completely free day out that celebrates the joy of cycling and I hope to see families from every corner of the city joining us to enjoy the activities."
